note: Skeptic Shark / skeptical-researcher angle. Judged only against the draft text and NORTH STAR v4. Findings that do not serve a success criterion are tagged out-of-scope and kept low severity.

findings.section: Wave 14 — Attention contract; Wave 15 — High Seat fold
findings.criterion: 12 ALTITUDE CONTRACT (typed projection from one read-only engine function) and 13 PORTFOLIO AT A GLANCE (from EXISTING portfolio index WITHOUT walking project roots)
findings.message: The draft asserts three incompatible storage facts at once: (a) Wave 14’s projection is ONE pure function that “performs zero writes”; (b) NS requires every project to PUBLISH a typed attention projection; (c) Wave 15 answers portfolio-at-a-glance and badge fold from the existing no-walk index with no root walk and High Seat write_authority none. If the function only reads the project ledger, the High Seat must visit N project stores to obtain N projections — that is a root walk, which criterion 13 forbids. If projections are already in the portfolio index, something must write them there on state change — that is a publish/write path the pure-function gate explicitly forbids and that Wave 14 never owns. “DERIVED ingest fires on a live write” (Wave 2 A5) is an audit observation, not a designed publish seam that Wave 14/15 bind to. Until the plan names the single legal path (who materializes projection rows into the index, on what event, with what read API that is not a root walk), criteria 12 and 13 cannot both be true, and the Wave-15 badge/glances tests are unfalsifiable plumbing theater.

findings.criterion: Wave-0 kill gate (“stage commissioned, executed by Anchor, validated handback”) and criterion 3 (nothing runs until confirm; commission is real spend)
findings.message: Wave 3 treats G4 failure as an acceptable branch: “FAIL branch documented as direct-launch fallback with substrate integration named as its own follow-on scope.” Wave-0 and the product statement require Anchor to execute a confirmed commission and return a validated handback on a fresh project. A documented follow-on is not a pass. The draft never states that G4 FAIL is a plan HALT that blocks Waves 9–17, nor that the “direct-launch fallback” is in-scope, auth-ON tested, and dossier-joined the same way. As written, the executor wave can “done-when” with a FAIL verdict on file while later waves still claim end-to-end commission→handback. That is an unconfirmed-spend / fake-orchestration escape hatch against the kill gate.

findings.section: Wave 3 — BUILD-E; Wave 4 — step-type map; Wave 9 — Commission proposal; Wave 17 — Wave-0 kill gate
findings.criterion: 6 (one campaign exercises AT LEAST TWO different commissioned skills) and Wave-0 full loop
findings.message: Criterion 6 and Wave 17 require two different commissioned skills in one campaign. Wave 3 only proves “a real trio run” through job_runner/terminal_session/lanes for one confirmed commission shape. Wave 4’s step-type map names researchPrime, Crucible, Foreman, Gandalf, but Wave 3 never requires observed PID + returned handback for a second skill family. Non-goal forbids changing Crucible/Foreman/researchPrime internals; G5 may classify gates as REQUIRES-TRIO-CHANGE / INVISIBLE and exclude them from v1. The draft does not force Wave 17 to pick two skills that are both (a) executor-proven and (b) free of excluded HALTs. Skeptical default: the e2e will green on Foreman×2 or mock dispatch labels while researchPrime/Gandalf remain propose-only. That fails criterion 6 as written (“different commissioned skills”), not “two labels on one substrate path.”

findings.topic: G5 HALT exclusion vs handback loop
findings.section: Wave 4 — G5 HALT inventory; Wave 12 — Handback validation / reflection
findings.criterion: 4 (validated handback → REFLECTION RECEIPT + next-stage propose→confirm) and Wave-0
findings.message: Wave 4 invents an exit: any commission path classed INVISIBLE or REQUIRES-TRIO-CHANGE is “excluded from v1 in the Face,” while non-goals forbid trio internal changes. Wave 12 and Wave-0 still require a validated handback that produces reflection + next-stage proposal. The plan never intersects these: there is no locked, test-enforced skill set for which handback is EXTERNALLY-OBSERVABLE end-to-end under auth ON, and no rule that Wave 17 may only commission that set. Without that intersection table as a machine-readable gate, “validated handback” can be satisfied by a fixture handback while live commissions sit parked at invisible human gates — exactly the silent non-orchestration the North Star forbids.

findings.section: Wave 3 — BUILD-E; Wave 5 — Ledger spine; Wave 6 — Commission dossier
findings.criterion: 10 (roadmap_events has exactly ONE writer, proven by concurrency test)
findings.message: Wave 3 launches real runs and records observed PID / handback before Wave 5 creates the single-writer spine and Wave 6’s dossier key. The draft does not forbid Wave 3 from writing roadmap/bind/launch records via the pre-spine paths (including the A4 non-atomic pair Wave 2 only documents). Criterion 10 is not “eventually one writer after Wave 5”; a second writer that remains reachable from the executor is a permanent dual path. Wave 5’s CI check can only police the tree as of Wave 5+; it does not automatically delete or quarantine Wave 3’s launch write sites. Order the spine (and dossier transaction) before any production commission write, or name Wave 3 as fixture-only with zero durable roadmap_events side effects — the draft does neither.

findings.topic: envelope bound unnamed and calibration ungated
findings.section: Wave 4 — compile-cost calibration; Wave 8 — Session envelope; Property gates — boundedness
findings.criterion: 2 (one confirmed session ENVELOPE; exhaustion hard-stops; no per-sentence confirm)
findings.message: Criterion 2 and the confirmation-fatigue risk require a real envelope, not a slogan. Wave 4’s calibration “gates nothing,” yet Wave 8 “sizes from the Phase-1 calibration dataset as the default.” No numeric bound (dollars, tokens, compile count, reflection count) appears in the plan body; property-gate boundedness demands a named number plus a refusal path when exceeded. Exhaustion is described, but without a named unit and default, “hard stop” cannot be tested independently of whatever number an implementer invents. Calibration that gates nothing cannot authorize the envelope that authorizes all compiles and reflections — that is circular and unfalsifiable.

findings.criterion: 3 (confirm records who; nothing runs until confirm), 10 (one writer / no lost or duplicated ledger truth), risk of unconfirmed or double spend
findings.message: The hardening law in the draft states idempotence is real only if something re-invokes and asserts no change, and lists a repeat-invocation gate. Batch-confirm scaffolding, commission confirm, envelope confirm, and handback→reflection are all spend-adjacent identity events. No wave’s acceptance criteria require double-submit / re-delivery tests (second confirm does not launch a second run, does not mint a second job_id, does not emit a second reflection proposal). Without those, the concurrency hammer only proves append transport, not “exactly once” lifecycle identity. A skeptical reading: network retry or double-click creates two commissions or two reflections while every “one writer” test still passes.

findings.section: Wave 15–16 failure tables; Hardening-gate obligations — Failure-state table vocabulary
findings.criterion: 9 (AUTH ON, asserted on outcomes), 12–13 (unknown never collapsed; unreadable → unknown row), 11 (honest-unknown)
findings.message: The plan’s own emitted hardening law requires every surface-bearing wave to answer five dependency/backing states with status code AND user-visible text, and to keep unknown and empty as separate rows. Chamber UI and High Seat are the user-visible surfaces for criteria 7, 12, and 13. Their wave-local tables (loading / unreadable / unknown / empty; badge ambient containment) never map dependency-missing, dependency-slow-or-killed, dependency-returns-garbage, backing-store-unreadable, empty-but-valid. Portfolio index slow/killed/garbage is exactly how a “silently shorter list” or a false idle appears. Local named states without the required five-row surface table do not satisfy the plan’s own honesty gate, so “unknown never idle” remains prose.

findings.section: Wave 7 — Scaffolding authoring; Wave 10 — Progressive elaboration; Wave 12 — Reflection receipt
findings.criterion: 1 (coarse steps + Oranges annotations), 4 (reflection with Oranges prompts), 5 (progressive elaboration from those annotations)
findings.message: Waves 7/10/12 require Oranges annotation fields and prompts but never define a minimum content contract or a failing test for empty/boilerplate annotations. A compiler can emit `oranges: []` or stock placeholders, batch-confirm, and still pass “has Oranges fields.” Stage-start “targeted questions derived from Oranges” then degenerates to no-questions-derivable (a named state the plan already allows). That collapses progressive elaboration (criterion 5) and reflection foresight (criterion 4) into optional garnish while criterion 1 is green on schema shape. Skeptical-researcher bar: annotations must be non-empty, stage-specific, and sufficient to derive at least one elaboration question or an explicit offered researchPrime branch — proven by a negative test that rejects barren scaffolds.

findings.section: Wave 7 — Scaffolding authoring; risk taxonomy “scaffolding mistaken for a commissioned plan”
findings.criterion: Statement (steward AUTHORS scaffolding; stage work COMMISSIONED — never authored by steward) and risk taxonomy (scaffolding mistaken for commissioned plan)
findings.message: Wave 7 only stamps a provenance flag and asserts scaffolding is not routed through adversarial review. It does not require that commission/bind/executor paths REFUSE to treat a steward-authored scaffold step as if it were a commissioned plan artifact, nor that UI copy cannot present scaffold steps as “planned by Crucible/Foreman.” Labeling without a hard reject at the commission boundary fails the risk the North Star names. The mistaken-identity failure mode is enforcement, not metadata.

findings.topic: wake-up composition may re-ask via model
findings.criterion: 11 CONTINUITY (first message from ledger only; asks NO question whose answer is already recorded; dead run + missing handback NAMED)
findings.message: Wave 13 correctly bans model-invented facts and adds a no-re-ask guard, but never states that the first message is a pure deterministic render of ledger fields (template/composer with zero model calls). assembleBriefPacket is zero-model; the “first-message composer” is a separate deliverable with no such ban. A model can rephrase ledger truth into interrogatives the guard’s brittle string match misses, or omit naming the dead run / missing handback while still “proposing next step.” Criterion 11’s kill-everything-then-resume proof requires the wake-up path to be as model-free and field-complete as the brief packet join — the draft leaves a model-shaped hole exactly where continuity is claimed.

findings.topic: missing-handback and dead-run only in e2e fixture
findings.section: Wave 11 — Session-state truth; Wave 12 — Handback; Wave 13 — Rehydration; Wave 17 — kill gate
findings.criterion: 11 (dead mid-flight run and handback that never arrived — both NAMED, never silently absorbed); 8 (status reflects actual session state across park/restart/kill)
findings.message: Naming anomalies is concentrated in Wave 13/17 scenarios. Wave 11 proves kill→dead status; Wave 12 names handback-missing as a failure state; neither requires that a run can be mid-flight dead AND a separate handback-never-arrived coexist as first-class dossier/status facts before rehydration. Criterion 11 demands both anomalies in one resume proof, not two alternate stories. Without a durable “expected handback not received” ledger fact distinct from “no commission yet” and “handback-invalid,” silent absorption remains possible: empty dossier fields read as idle/unknown and the wake-up test is fed a hand-built fixture the product loop never writes.

findings.criterion: 9–11 (outcome-asserted durability, continuity, single writer) and plan’s own law (“claim without matching obligation is a BLOCKER”)
findings.message: The draft ends with durability/honesty/idempotence/boundedness/containment gates as unchecked boxes and repeated obligation lists, while waves claim atomic write, locks, concurrency, honest-unknown, and bounds. No wave done-when closes a specific checkbox; containment (escape-attempt for `..` / absolute / symlink) and idempotence (repeat-invocation) have no owning wave deliverable at all. Per the draft’s journal-0080 rule, a property claimed without a matching enforceable gate is a blocker-class plan defect. Leaving the emitted checklist empty while advertising hardening is exactly the “validating a rule is not providing it” failure the plan quotes.

findings.section: Wave 15 — High Seat fold / portfolio at a glance
findings.message: Wave 15 says the glance is answered from engine/portfolio/query.mjs, but Wave 2’s A5 only audits liveness and DERIVED ingest — it does not prove the index already carries campaign stage, run liveness, and last movement at the grain criterion 13 requires. Non-goal forbids rebuilding the index; fix-items are allowed. The draft never requires the A5 coverage table to list, field-by-field, whether stage / live|waiting|blocked / last_movement are present today, and never schedules fix-items for each missing field before Wave 15. If those fields are absent, Wave 15 will either re-walk project roots (forbidden), invent a side cache (second source of truth), or show a thinner list — all

findings.topic: unattended reflection vs live-envelope debit rules
findings.section: Wave 8 — Session envelope; Wave 12 — unattended handback queue
findings.criterion: 2 (envelope covers orchestrator-loop reflections) and 4 (on validated handback, emit reflection + propose next stage)
findings.message: Gate Decision 1 queues unattended reflections with zero spend; Wave 12 then compiles + proposes at next session open, debiting the live envelope. Criterion 4’s happy path assumes a reflection receipt on validated handback; the draft does not specify whether “queued reflection” counts as having satisfied criterion 4’s emit, or only after session-open compile. If tests treat queue as success, overnight handbacks never produce the receipt artifact until John opens a session — acceptable for spend, but then criterion 4 must be restated as “queued or emitted.” If tests require immediate receipt, they contradict Decision 1. The plan leaves that contradiction unresolved.

findings.criterion: 3 tests reject fabricated display names. The draft allows the FAIL branch but does not require UI/outcome assertions that who is visibly non-identity. Skeptical residual: auth-ON green with a shared secret still looks like a named principal.
findings.message: Recording `unattributed(shared_secret)` as who satisfies the field shape while collapsing multi-operator accountability to a shared credential class. Acceptable as an honest FAIL of subject recovery only if every spend UI and audit log renders that weakness permanently and
The locked North Star is pasted in full twice, then restated again as bullet success criteria. Harmless to runtime truth but increases drift risk between copies; not a North Star criterion failure.

findings.topic: Face glossary ASR out of scope vs “spoken”
findings.criterion: 1 and 7 (“spoken description” / “spoken correction” as typed NL per glossary)
findings.message: The plan correctly defines talking as typed NL and ASR out of scope, but still uses “spoken” in deliverables and done-whens. Low severity if tests accept typed NL; still a false-requirement trap for implementers who build ASR. Align vocabulary to “typed NL description/correction” everywhere criterion language is operationalized.
